line: Oh, you said that you the big shotta? The don dada? Boom, boom, shaka-laka, meet this big chopper
vault_lines: Oh, you said that you the big shotta? The don dada?
meaning:
Proclaiming himself as king of New York City, 6ix9ine disses fellow New York native Lil Mabu, who has also proclaimed himself the king of NYC—notably in his May 2023 track, “MATHEMATICAL DISRESPECT.”

6ix9ine specifically alludes to Mabu’s June 2023 track “RICH SCHOLAR,” where he rapped:

I’m a rich scholar, rich scholar
Top Shotta, Don Dada
I’m a rich scholar, got the city shook

These lyrics also exploit 6ix9ine’s previous gang affiliations, as a choppa is a slang term for an automatic firearm.

line: Nigga, how you lose your bitch to a snitch?
vault_lines: Nigga, how you lose your bitch to a snitch?
meaning:
Kodak is dissing Puerto Rican rapper Anuel AA. The mother of Anuel’s child



Anuel and Yailin La Mas Viral, who is also featured on this track, were previously married and have a child together, and now she is dating 6ix9ine just a few months after the announcement of their divorce.



Despite previously collaborating on the tracks “Bebe” and “Mala,” 6ix9ine and Anuel have been beefing for quite some time now. This stems from Tekashi’s reputation as a snitch. Anuel collaborated with 6ix9ine on Tekashi’s post-prison release “Yaya,” however, Anuel’s verse was cut from the released version. They recently reinitiated their feud after going back and forth on their Instagram stories 2 weeks ago, with Yailin being in the center of the beef.

For further context, Anuel previously collaborated with Kodak on the track “Sufro”, which features fellow Puerto Rican rapper Ñengo Flow.



Just 7 months following the release of the song, Kodak is now collaborating with 6ix9ine and starting his verse with this line, creating even more controversy.
